newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bond issue seen helping telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bond issue seen helping telecom sale.

text.p: A $150 million five-year bond exchangeable into shares of state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd (PTCL) will help in PTCL's privatisation, government officials and analysts said on Friday.

Nomura International Plc and Union Bank of Switzerland have jointly launched meetings, known as roadshows, to generate investor interest abroad for the bond, which will be issued by the Pakistani government, Khalil Masood, chairman of the state Corporate Law Authority, told Reuters on Friday.
"The bond issue will help in the privatisation of the PTCL," Masood said.
Ali Raza, a dealer on the Karachi Stock Exchange, said, "This sale will generate interest among foreign investors, who are planning to participate in the PTCL privatisation."
Arif Habib, president of the exchange, said the bond was likely to attract a good price ahead of PTCL's privatisation.
Pricing is scheduled after conclusion of the roadshow in Singapore on February 18, another government official said.
While Prime minister-designate Nawaz Sharif has not given the schedule for the privatisation, it is likely in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June), Raza said.
In 1994, the government floated PTCL's 12 percent stake in the local market in the form of common stocks and abroad as global depositary receipt (GDR).

Many investors bought PTCL shares at 55 rupees in 1994 and 1995 but its price fluctuated between 33.15 and 36 in the past few days. The lower price had eroded the investment of investors who bought at 55.
Habib said raising the conversion premium higher than the indicative rate of 7.5 percent was likely to lift the stock price on local bourses.
"Competitive bidding is important to protect the interest of many existing shareholders who bought its shares at 55 rupees," he said.
The dollar denominated five-year maturity bond will have a coupon rate indicated at six percent payable semi-annually with an issuer call option at par from February 2000.
The issue also has a three-year investors' put option at a price to yield 150 basis points above the three-year U.S. treasuries.
The bond would be listed at the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and the investor will have the option to exchange them into common stock listed in Pakistani bourses or into GDRs.
Habib said, the rate of premium on the bond and the government's commitment to privatise PTCL will benefit the bond holders.

He said the government would benefit during the privatisation of PTCL if its share rose on the local bourses. The share price would automatically rise if the conversion premium of the bond was raised through competitive bidding.

"It will be in the interest of government to maintain higher prices of the PTCL shares at the stock market so that it can get better price against the sale of shares through the privatisation processe. That can only be possible through the conversion feature of the bonds," he added.
PTCL "A" 10-rupee scrip closed 0.15 lower at 32.85 and its voucher 1.85 down at 33.15 at the KSE on Thursday.
